claim: In the Malaysia recruitment of 2022 to 2024, workers went through recruiting agencies picked for the syndicate, and many who reached Malaysia got no job
A survey of 357 migrants in Malaysia by Verite and four other organisations found workers paid BDT 544,000 on average, against a government-fixed cost of BDT 79,000
Selim of Narayanganj went to Malaysia, was put on construction piling work instead of the job promised, was injured, got no treatment from the company and bought his own ticket home
Around the 31 May 2024 Malaysia deadline, workers who had paid BDT 500,000 to 600,000 were stuck at Dhaka airport without air tickets although BMET clearance and visas had been obtained
After the 31 May 2024 deadline many agencies could not be reached by phone and some offices were shut
35 workers who went to Russia in July 2025 with BMET clearance returned on 18 January 2026 after losing their jobs
Those workers were placed with a different company from the one named on their BMET clearance and made to do construction work instead of factory work
Each of those workers had spent about BDT 700,000 on average to go to Russia
A man who flew to Russia on 7 May 2026 had gone through a recruiting agency in Malibagh, Dhaka, with BMET clearance, for a company job
The group of 30 was kept three days in a hotel in Russia and then handed to the army
He paid BDT 700,000 and his wife says none of it has come back
A man who went to Cambodia for a data-entry job had a written contract on BDT 200 stamp paper
He attended three days of BMET training at Probashi Kalyan Bhaban in Dhaka and received BMET clearance (the smart card)
He was taken to a walled scam compound near the Thai border, where his phone and passport were taken
He paid USD 3,200 for his release, and the broker who had promised compensation disappeared and closed his office

A survivors' organisation told the Expatriates' Welfare Ministry on 18 October 2026 that about 1,800 Bangladeshi workers who went to Cambodia with valid passports, visas and government clearance were forced to work in online scam compounds
The state minister for expatriates' welfare told Parliament in June 2026 that nominal companies abroad bring in 100 people where there is work for 10
The ministry wants demand letters checked more strictly at embassy level
The 30 men who flew to Russia on 7 May 2026 had valid visas, job contracts and BMET clearance, and were sent by licensed recruiting agencies
In Russia on 12 May the men were made to sign a contract in Russian, told it was for a bank card, SIM card and work permit; it was a contract to join the Russian army
